# <span id="aanchor326"></span> Exception Resolver

[Overview](Exception%20Resolver.md) \| [Exception Grid](Exception%20Resolver_Grid.md) \| [Object Explorer](Exception%20Resolver_Object%20Explorer.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Notes</a> \| [Settings](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md)

## Notes

Exceptions may require supplemental documentation to provide additional status information.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

Validations for a meter are set so that exceptions are generated when the flow data temperature falls below 55°F. An analyst can change the status of these exceptions to "Acknowledged" during the time frames that fall outside of the validation range, and provide an edit reason for doing so. A senior analyst would like to see some documentation inside FLOWCAL that describes the meter data conditions and provides context for why FLOWCAL reports data discrepancies.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Creating Notes">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Creating Notes</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Creating Notes">

You can add notes to objects that exceptions are associated with directly from the Exception Resolver grid.

<div class="procedure">

To add a note to an object in the Exception Resolver:

1.  Highlight the desired exceptions.

2.  Click the **Add Note** icon 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="vertical-align: text-top;width: 21;height: 19;" />on the toolbar.

    You can also right-click one of the highlighted exceptions and select **Add Note** or **View Notes**. When the View Notes screen displays, you can then click the **Add Note** button.

3.  When the Add Note screen displays, provide the required data:
    - **First Date** - The beginning effective date for the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the minimum effective date of the exceptions selected in the exception grid.

    - **Last Date** - The ending effective date for the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the maximum effective date of the exceptions selected in the exception grid.

    - **Visibility** - Designation to determine who can view the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the user’s visibility settings in User Preferences window. Other options are:
      - **Everyone** - All FLOWCAL users can access the note.
      - **Internal** - All FLOWCAL users can access the note, but the note will not display on any standard reports.
      - **Private** - Only the user who created the note can view it.

    - **Expiration Date** - Date after which the note will no longer be visible in FLOWCAL. (The record of the note will still be stored in the database.)

       The Expired Notes report can be used to view a list of expired notes in FLOWCAL.

    - **Custom Fields** - Four custom text boxes are available for capturing additional data. (If custom fields are configured on the Notes tab of the [Custom Fields Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Custom%20Fields.md), those fields will be generated when you first open the Add Note screen.)

    - **Note Text** - The documentation portion of the note (required).

    - **Object Information** - The number, name and type of any objects associated with the selected exceptions.

       If you click the delete button on any of the object rows, the note will no longer be included on that object.

    - When you have finished entering the note date, click **Done**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 549;height: 410;" />

After a note is saved, a note icon will display next to the exception(s) you selected if the effective date for the exception(s) falls within the date range of the note.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 401;height: 96;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Viewing Notes">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Viewing Notes</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Viewing Notes">

To view notes associated with an object:

Right-click an exception with a note icon and select **View Notes**.

When the View Notes screen displays, you will be able to view the full body of the note, as well as the following Object History details:

- **Modified Date** - GMS date when the note was last edited.
- **Modified By** - Name of the user who last edited the note.
- **First Date\*** - Effective starting date of the note.
- **Last Date\*** - Effective ending date of the note.
- **Expiration Date\*** - Date after which the note will no longer be available.
- **Visibility\*** - Designation indicating who can view the note.
- **Custom 1–4** - Editable fields used to capture additional data. (If custom fields are configured on the notes tab of the [Custom Fields Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Custom%20Fields.md), the column headers in the View Notes screen will match those custom fields.)

\* These items are read-only; they are only editable in the Add Note screen.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 562;height: 420;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Deleting Notes">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Deleting Notes</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Deleting Notes">

Notes are deleted from the Object History grid.

<div class="procedure">

To delete a note:

1.  Hover over a note in the Object History grid.
2.  Click the delete button when it displays.

Deleting a note removes the note from the object. Any exceptions for the object within the effective date range of the note will no longer include the note icon.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Column Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Column Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Column Options">

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options:

- **Sort Ascending** - Sort items in ascending order for the selected column.
- **Sort Descending** - Sort items in descending order for the selected column.
- **Show Column Chooser** - Open the Column Selector to select the columns to display in the grid. (See: [Column Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector))
- **Best Fit** - Expand the selected column to display the complete contents.
- **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expand all columns to display the complete contents.
- **Filter Editor** - Open the Filter Editor to create conditional statements based on any column or value within the column.

##### Column Order

To change the order of the columns, click a column header and then drag and drop the column to the new location.

You can remove a column by dragging and dropping it outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save this layout when you exit the screen.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sorting Notes">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sorting Notes</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Sorting Notes">

By default, notes are sorted by modified date, in descending order.

<div class="procedure">

To change the sort order of notes:

- Click any column header to sort notes by that parameter.
- Click a header again to reverse the list order (ascending or descending).
- Right-click a column header and select **Sort Ascending** or **Sort Descending**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Filtering Notes">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Filtering Notes</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Filtering Notes">

You can filter notes by a single column or by multiple columns.

<div class="procedure">

To filter by a single column:

1.  Hover over a column header to display the filter icon.
2.  Click the filter icon to open the Filter dialog box. The dialog box contains two tabs:
    - **Filter Values** - Select the values that you want to display.
    - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example: "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). Select the condition, and then specify a value.
3.  Close the Filter dialog box by clicking on the grid.
4.  After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter.

To filter by multiple columns, right-click a column header and select **Filter Editor**.

The following example shows a filter that uses multiple columns:



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 668;height: 419;" />

</div>

</div>
